_notes: POST /v1/payments/initiate needs a tenant token and the orders:create entitlement. It calls Paystack live — use a Paystack TEST secret key in QA.

Webhooks are unauthenticated but signature-verified. An invalid signature returns HTTP 200 with {received:true} and does NOTHING — 200 is not proof of processing, always verify the side effect in the DB / GET /v1/orders/{id}.
Routing is by data.metadata.schemaName. Without it the handler no-ops. schemaName is 't_' + tenantId with dashes replaced by underscores.
Paystack signature: HMAC-SHA512 of the RAW body with PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY, sent as x-paystack-signature.
Flutterwave signature: the verif-hash header compared against FLUTTERWAVE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
Replay of the same reference must be idempotent — the second delivery is skipped as a duplicate.

_signing_commands.paystack: BODY=$(cat paystack_charge_success.json); SIG=$(printf '%s' "$BODY" | openssl dgst -sha512 -hmac "$PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY" | awk '{print $2}'); curl -sS -X POST $BASE/v1/payments/webhook/paystack -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "x-paystack-signature: $SIG" --data-raw "$BODY"
_signing_commands.tamper_check: Re-send either request with one digit of the signature changed — expect 200 {received:true} and NO change to the order or payment row.
